answer: Every bolt of sailcloth is stamped at the loft before it is cut, and the register holds the stamp of each bolt beside the weaver's name. A cipher bolt claimed as stamped fails the register: the stamp must match the loft's own seal at the jade of the cloth, and a bolt never stamped is only grey canvas. Forging a stamp means bribing the loft keeper, faking a year of entries and paying 12,600, and the zephyr register is kept until the sail wears out, so cloth whose bolt was never stamped is cut up for rags.
